fatal_errors: The proposed ML-optimized spark plasma sintering method is unrelated to the target liquid-metal dealloying process in molten Cu.

The hypothesis seeks a homogeneous, segregation-suppressed composite, whereas the target deliberately exploits directional Ti/V-rich segregation to form a bicontinuous RHEA-ligament/Cu-channel architecture.
It omits the essential 1200 °C, 96 h molten-Cu immersion condition and the directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor.
Its kinetic suppression mechanism does not match selective Ti–Cu exchange, dissolution of sacrificial interdendritic regions, and formation of a W-rich passivating interlayer.
It does not predict or address the target thermal-conductivity and helium-irradiation outcomes.
Neither cited source supports ML optimization, SPS processing of RHEA–Cu composites, or the claimed suppression of Cu–refractory phase separation.
explanation: The response recognizes only the broad challenge of processing RHEA–Cu materials with unfavorable mixing thermodynamics. It otherwise proposes a different and unevidenced processing route. The hidden work uses liquid-metal dealloying to exploit, rather than suppress, precursor segregation: molten Cu selectively replaces Ti-rich interdendritic channels while continuous W/Ta/V-rich ligaments remain, with a W-rich interfacial layer stabilizing the composite. No target-specific composition, reaction condition, architecture, interface, thermal performance, or irradiation result is reconstructed. The proposed comparison between conventional and ML-optimized SPS is experimentally falsifiable, so experiment discriminability is relatively good for the alternative hypothesis itself, but it does not discriminate or validate the mechanism reported in the target. The cited evidence concerns general RHEA properties and additive manufacturing and provides no valid support for the SPS/ML claims.
